messages.subject: Covariates in scanone/scantwo
parts:
Hi,

How are covariates with more than two levels treated in scanone and
scantwo? In my case, I have 4 levels that represent an continuous
gradient. Because they are forced to be a number in scanone, I suspect
that they are treated as.numeric in the model. However, I know suspect
that there are non-linear effects of the QTL from running scanone within
each environment. Thus, I would like to be able to treat my covariate
as a factor. Is this possible?

Thanks,
Alan

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: Covariates in scanone/scantwo
parts:
If you have a 4-level factor as a covariate, you need to
explicitly code the 3 covariate columns for your model.

If "f" is the factor, you might write:

x <- as.numeric(f)
m <- matrix(0, ncol=length(levels(f))-1, nrow=length(f))
for(i in 1:(length(levels(f))-1))
m[x==i,i] <- 1

Then use the "m" matrix as the covariate.

karl

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: Covariates in scanone/scantwo
parts:
You can. All of the covariates in scanone() and scantwo()
must be strictly numeric. You can make a single column, or
you can expand it to several columns, but the expansion is
not yet done automatically.

karl
